keywords.def: (informal) using banned substances to perform better in a sports competition
used to introduce a statement which the speaker believes is balanced, reasonable or true
causing disagreement and argument between people
start behaving in an unacceptable way
behave in a way that encourages others to behave well/badly
treat something as normal or acceptable when it previously was not

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Pippa. Sharing your Netflix password, lying about your age or not paying the bus fare are a few examples of cheating in daily life.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是皮帕。在日常生活中，共享Netflix密码、隐瞒年龄或逃公交车票都是作弊的例子。

sentences.en: But there's one place where cheating is usually considered wrong, and that's sport.
sentences.zh: 但有一个地方作弊通常被认为是错误的，那就是体育。

sentences.en: Cheating in sport through the use of performance-enhancing drugs, informally called doping, is normally considered wrong.
sentences.zh: 在体育运动中通过使用兴奋剂（通常称为doping）来作弊，通常被认为是错误的。

sentences.en: Just ask American cycling legend Lance Armstrong, who was thrown out of the sport for using banned substances.
sentences.zh: 去问问美国自行车传奇人物兰斯·阿姆斯特朗（Lance Armstrong）就知道了，他因使用违禁药物而被驱逐出这项运动。

sentences.en: But earlier this year, a sporting event took place which turned the debate about drugs in sport upside down.
sentences.zh: 但今年早些时候，一项体育赛事颠覆了关于体育界药物使用的争论。

sentences.en: Here's Asma Khalid from BBC World Service's The Global Story to explain: This weekend, elite athletes from around the world are descending on Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first-of-its-kind sporting competition known as The Enhanced Games.
sentences.zh: 听听来自BBC世界新闻频道《全球故事》的阿斯玛·哈alid（Asma Khalid）的解释：这个周末，来自世界各地的精英运动员正涌向内华达州拉斯维加斯，参加这场独一无二的、被称为“增强运动会”（The Enhanced Games）的体育比赛。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the Olympics, but only for swimming, sprinting and weightlifting.
sentences.zh: 这有点像奥运会，但只设游泳、短跑和举重项目。

sentences.en: The aim is to break world records. In fact, some of these competitors are former Olympians – medallists battling it out for money and glory.
sentences.zh: 目的是打破世界纪录。事实上，其中一些参赛者是前奥运选手——奖牌得主们为了金钱和荣耀展开对决。

sentences.en: But there's one big difference... The big difference is that The Enhanced Games allow athletes to use performance-enhancing drugs that are banned in professional sports.
sentences.zh: 但有一个巨大的区别……最大的区别在于，“增强运动会”允许运动员使用在职业体育中被禁用的兴奋剂。

sentences.en: In these games, nicknamed The Doping Olympics, steroids, growth hormones and stimulants are all OK.
sentences.zh: 在这场被称为“兴奋剂奥运会”的比赛中，类固醇、生长激素和兴奋剂都是允许的。

sentences.en: You're a big sports fan, Neil. Would you enjoy watching a sport where the athletes have taken drugs?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，你是个超级体育迷。你会喜欢看运动员服用药物的比赛吗？

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't. I really don't think that's fair.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会。我真的认为这不公平。

sentences.en: I think we need to know that all the athletes start and compete from the same level.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要知道所有运动员都在同一起跑线上开始和竞争。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I don't really watch that many sports so I guess I wouldn't notice the difference, but if you're really into sport you care about the rules, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这说得通。我其实不怎么看体育比赛，所以我想我不会注意到区别，但如果你真的很热爱体育，你会在乎规则，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely. And in this episode we'll dive into the controversial world of The Enhanced Games, learning some useful new words and phrases along the way.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对的。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨“增强运动会”这个充满争议的世界，并在过程中学习一些有用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary, plus a quiz and a worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇、一个小测验以及一份练习表。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有一个问题要问你，尼尔。

sentences.en: You mentioned the famous sporting cheat Lance Armstrong, but how many times did Lance Armstrong win the famous race, the Tour de France, before he was finally caught out?
sentences.zh: 你提到了著名的体育作弊者兰斯·阿姆斯特朗（Lance Armstrong），但在他最终被抓之前，他赢了多少次著名的环法自行车赛（Tour de France）？

sentences.en: Was it: a) five, b) six, or c) seven? Ooh...
sentences.zh: 是：a) 五次，b) 六次，还是 c) 七次？哦……

sentences.en: Well, it was a lot, so I think I'll go for c) seven.
sentences.zh: 嗯，次数很多，所以我想我选 c) 七次。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, it's no exaggeration to say that The Enhanced Games are controversial.
sentences.zh: 现在，毫不夸张地说，“增强运动会”充满争议。

sentences.en: After all, organisations like the World Anti- Doping Agency have spent decades fighting performance-enhancing drugs in sport.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，像世界反兴奋剂机构（World Anti-Doping Agency）这样的组织已经花了数十年时间在体育界打击兴奋剂。

sentences.en: Here's BBC sports editor Dan Roan on World Service programme The Global Story.
sentences.zh: 听听BBC体育编辑丹·罗恩（Dan Roan）在世界服务节目《全球故事》中的看法。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say it's one of the most divisive and controversial events that the world of sport has seen for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，这是体育界长期以来见过的最具分裂性和争议性的赛事之一。

sentences.en: It's an event where performance-enhancing drugs, banned elsewhere in mainstream sport of course, are actually allowed to be taken by the competitors under medical supervision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在主流体育运动中被禁用的兴奋剂，实际上允许参赛者在医疗监督下服用的赛事。

sentences.en: Dan Roan says, " It's fair to say The Enhanced Games are controversial." He uses the phrase it's fair to say to introduce a statement that he considers to be balanced and reasonable – that the games are controversial.
sentences.zh: 丹·罗恩说：“公平地说，‘增强运动会’充满争议。”他用“公平地说”这个短语来引出一个他认为是平衡且合理的陈述——即这些运动会充满争议。

sentences.en: Dan also describes the games as divisive – an adjective that means causing a lot of disagreement between people.
sentences.zh: 丹还将这些运动会描述为“具分裂性的”——这是一个形容词，意指在人们之间引起很多分歧。

sentences.en: Much of this disagreement is about the use of performance-enhancing drugs themselves.
sentences.zh: 这种分歧很大程度上是关于使用兴奋剂本身。

sentences.en: The Games' organisers point out that all drugs are approved by the US Food and Drug Agency and taken openly under medical supervision, which they say makes them safer than when they are taken secretly at competitions elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 运动会的组织者指出，所有药物都获得了美国食品药品监督管理局（US Food and Drug Agency）的批准，并在医疗监督下公开服用，他们认为这比在其他比赛中秘密服用更安全。

sentences.en: But there are many critics too, as Dan Roan outlined to BBC World Service's The Global Story.
sentences.zh: 但也有许多批评者，正如丹·罗恩向BBC世界服务频道的《全球故事》所阐述的那样。

sentences.en: But the critics, of course, say that this crosses an ethical line, that it sets a dreadful example because it risks normalising doping.
sentences.zh: 但批评者当然表示，这越过了道德底线，树立了一个可怕的榜样，因为它有使兴奋剂常规化的风险。

sentences.en: It could harm the integrity, therefore, of sport, and it could be dangerous to the health of those taking part.
sentences.zh: 因此，它可能会损害体育的公正性，并可能危及参赛者的健康。

sentences.en: For the Games' critics, doping crosses an ethical line.
sentences.zh: 对于运动会的批评者来说，使用兴奋剂越过了道德底线。

sentences.en: The phrase to cross the line means to start behaving in a way that's not socially acceptable.
sentences.zh: “越过底线”这个短语意味着开始表现出不被社会接受的行为。

sentences.en: These critics say the Games set a bad example, meaning that they encourage others to behave badly as well.
sentences.zh: 这些批评者表示，运动会树立了一个坏榜样，意味着它们鼓励其他人也做出糟糕的行为。

sentences.en: Why is that, Pippa? Well, it's because critics argue the games normalise the use of performance drugs in sport.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，皮帕？嗯，这是因为批评者认为，这些运动会使体育运动中兴奋剂的使用常规化。

sentences.en: If you normalise something, you treat it as normal or acceptable when previously it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 如果你将某事常规化，你就会在以前不被接受的时候，把它当作正常或可接受的事情来对待。

sentences.en: But with arguments strongly held on both sides, the debate is far from over.
sentences.zh: 但由于双方观点坚决，这场辩论远未结束。

sentences.en: So Neil, have you changed your opinion after hearing both sides of the story?
sentences.zh: 那么尼尔，听了双方的说法后，你改变看法了吗？

sentences.en: No, I haven't. I think it's just not fair, and I think if you're not fair in sport, what's the point?
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。我认为这根本不公平，而且我认为如果在体育中不公平，那还有什么意义？

sentences.en: Well, let's hear the answer to my quiz question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们听听我的测验题的答案吧，尼尔。

sentences.en: I asked you how many times Lance Armstrong won the Tour de France, and it was c) seven times, consecutively between 1999 and 2005.
sentences.zh: 我问你兰斯·阿姆斯特朗（Lance Armstrong）赢了多少次环法自行车赛，答案是 c) 七次，在1999年至2005年期间连续夺冠。

sentences.en: Of course, we now know that there were performance-enhancing drugs involved.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现在知道其中涉及使用兴奋剂。

sentences.en: OK. So, now it's time to recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with doping – using banned drugs to perform better in sporting competitions.
sentences.zh: 好的。那么，现在是时候复习我们学过的词汇了，首先是doping（兴奋剂/使用禁药）——在体育比赛中为了表现更好而使用违禁药物。

sentences.en: You can use the phrase it's fair to say to introduce a statement you consider to be balanced, reasonable or true.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用短语“公平地说”来引出一个你认为是平衡、合理或真实的陈述。

sentences.en: If something is divisive, it causes disagreement between people.
sentences.zh: 如果某事是“具分裂性的”（divisive），它会在人们之间引起分歧。

sentences.en: The idiom cross the line means to start behaving in an unacceptable way.
sentences.zh: 习语“越过底线”（cross the line）意味着开始以不可接受的方式行事。

sentences.en: If you set a bad example, you behave in a way that encourages others to behave badly.
sentences.zh: 如果你“树立了一个坏榜样”（set a bad example），你的行为就会鼓励其他人也表现不好。

sentences.en: And finally, to normalise something means to treat it as normal or acceptable when previously it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 最后，“使……常规化”（normalise）意味着在以前不正常或不可接受的时候，将其视为正常或可接受的。

sentences.en: OK. Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to practise more, you'll find a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 好的。我们的6分钟又到了，但如果你想练习更多，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到一个小测验和练习表。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见。但现在，再见。

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
